brief: A wall clock with hands that turn and tell the time.

requirements.evidence: No clock movement, motor, dial, or hand part exists in the Hex Cluster catalog (searched clock, hand, dial, motor; 174 props contain no clock). The pencil (prop:1) and pen (prop:2) laid on the cover are static staging props, not powered parts, so they cannot turn or tell time.
requirements.requirement: Hands that turn and tell the time

requirements.evidence: Single full hex base (piece:0,0,0;full) with full top cover as the dial face, pencil and pen posed as hour/minute hands angled apart, visible from above (look polar 10 sees both props). Static pose only, readable as a clock face but not functional.
requirements.requirement: Wall clock face reading as a clock

requirements.evidence: accessory:0#0,0#0 hex-acc-keyhole keyhole hanger on the cell; caps on open faces, lockJoints applied; check_build ok with meshClash clear.

finish.summary: Built a single-hex wall plaque with keyhole hanger and a cover dial face with pen/pencil hands. No moving clock mechanism exists in the Hex Cluster catalog or props, so turning/time-telling hands are unmet; the hands are static staging posed to suggest a time.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Building a working wall clock — hands that actually tell time.
